messages:
carla: Quick sync 1: we need to pick a model for fallback arbitration: score-fusion vs rule-first. leaning towards a small deterministic scoring function so we can explain why a variant was evicted.
noah: Score-fusion + thresholding. It lets us combine error-rate, latency penalty, and degradation velocity (how fast errors are rising). Rules only are too brittle.
reena: Agree on explainability but also on boundedness. If we use scores we must clamp influence so a noisy spike in one host doesn't evict globally. Suggest per-tenant hysteresis + vote window.
dmitri: Concrete: compute per-variant score S = w1*err_pct_norm + w2*latency_norm + w3*trend_norm + w4*cost_penalty. Then apply two-stage policy: 1) local short-window check (3m) with high-sensitivity but only applies to local shard; 2) global fused decision (5m) from controller that requires score > G for at least M consecutive windows.
carla: That aligns. We also need "soft-fallback" vs "hard-evict" semantics. Soft-fallback = route new sessions away but keep existing sessions. Hard-evict = force immediate switch.
noah: UX: make soft default for A-B experiments, hard only for canaries with safety guarantees. Also expose both counters in Console.
reena: Telemetry implications: soft-fallback needs per-session routing tags and sticky-cookie propagation. We should record "session_migration" events.
canarybot: canary: started experiment id=exp-2026-03-21-12:03 size=4% region=eu-west :seedling:
dmitri: We must be careful about feedback loops: if soft-fallback reduces traffic to variant, metrics drop and score improves -> oscillation. Solution: decay-rollout window and min-quorum sample requirement (don't trust score if sample_count < N).
carla: Good point. Add min_q=200 requests/5m per-variant to surface for global decisions.
noah: For ties or near-ties, prefer the lower-cost variant unless S difference < epsilon, then no action. This keeps costs predictable.
reena: Let's add a cost-aware penalty to prevent promoting high-cost variants for minor improvements. Also add a per-team budget override flag to allow paid experiments.
dmitri: Implementation note: controller exposes /v1/decision-log with entries: timestamp, variant_id, score, sample_count, decision. Local runtime pulls down recent decision fragments and can prefetch the controller's last decision for reconciliation.
carla: Example manifest extension idea:
```yaml
experiment:
  arbitration:
    algorithm: score_fusion
    weights: [0.5, 0.2, 0.2, 0.1] # err, latency, velocity, cost
    soft_fallback: true
    min_sample_count: 200
    global_window_minutes: 5
    local_fast_window_seconds: 30
    cost_bias_threshold: 0.03 # only override if score delta > 3%
```
noah: Tests: add a synthetic workload that simulates cold-start latency spike plus gradual error ramp, and assert the system picks soft-fallback first then escalates if trend persists.
reena: Observability: new Console charts: per-variant score curve, sample_count, and recommended-action. Also add an anomaly badge when sample_count < min_sample_count.
dmitri: Security: decisions must be authenticated and carry provenance. sign controller decisions with keyrotate header. Runtimes should reject unsigned overrides.
carla: Ops playbook: when a hard-evict occurs, auto-create a rollback ticket with links to top-5 traces and the decision log snippet. That helps oncall triage.
canarybot: canary: exp-2026-03-21 now at 4% steady state 12:06 :white_check_mark:
noah: open question: do we allow per-variant custom weights? some teams want latency-first experiments.
reena: Allow per-team overrides but validate against central guardrails. If a team's weights would increase expected cost over budget, require approval.
dmitri: Action items: 1) draf tscore-fusion proto + decision-log schema 1@dmitri, 2) manifest PR with arbitration fields @noah, 3) Console prototypes for score curve @reena, 4) add chaos test for oscillation cases @carla.
carla: I'll file the RFC addendum and link this thread. Thanks everyone. :pray:
